q: Build the full amplitude-amplification exact-QFT circuit for p=7 (Kitaev eigenvalue-estimation + uniformisation register + reflections around |0> and P_good) end-to-end in Qiskit, and verify the resulting unitary matches DFT_7 to ~1e-12. Does the paper's 'six applications of A' bound (Sec. 2.2) hold as gate count, depth, or as coarser query complexity?
basis: Our replication exercised the *target* DFT_N unitary directly rather than the amplitude-amplification construction the paper introduces. The paper's actual contribution is an existence proof; a live gate-level circuit that hits DFT_7 to machine precision would be the true operational replication.
next_steps: Implement Kitaev eigenvalue-estimation on the cyclic-shift U|x>=|(x+1) mod p> for p=7 in Qiskit; wrap in amplitude amplification (Brassard-Hoyer style) with uniformisation register r ~ Unif(0..6); measure Operator(qc) fidelity to DFT_7; count 1q/2q gates and T-depth after Solovay-Kitaev synthesis.

q: The average success probability p_bar(p, N) approaches 0.451412 from above with a residual that decays like c/p at large N (our data: 0.4519 at p=1021, 0.4514 in the integral limit). What is the exact leading coefficient c, and does it depend on the fractional part of log_2(N/p)?
basis: Our results_pbar.json shows monotone convergence with a clear ~1/p asymptotic, but we did not derive the coefficient analytically. This matters for the Sec. 4.2 uniformisation-qubit angle alpha at small primes.
next_steps: Expand f^2 in powers of 1/p using the Euler-Maclaurin correction to the Riemann sum; extract the O(1/p) term as a closed-form integral of f^2 derivatives; compare against numeric fit to our convergence table.

q: For composite order q (Sec. 5.1's phi(q)/q regime), which (c, d) measurement outcomes leak the discrete log only modulo divisors of q rather than modulo q itself, and can this partial information be combined across O(log q) runs to recover a even when no single run has gcd(d, q) = 1?
basis: Our initial (wrong-convention) run with r = p - 1 = 6 for p = 7 showed the distribution concentrating on d in {0, 2, 4} - exactly the divisor-of-6 structure that Sec. 5.1 alludes to. The paper punts on this to a 'more involved solution' (Sec. 5.1.1) without simulation.
next_steps: For q in {6, 8, 15, 21}: enumerate the joint (c, d) distribution for random a; classify outcomes by gcd(d, q); implement Sec. 5.1.1's O(log q) recovery loop; measure end-to-end success prob and mean number of quantum runs.

q: How many bits of precision on the rotation angle alpha in Sec. 4.2's uniformisation qubit are required to keep the amplitude-amplification success probability within 1e-6 of the target 1/4, and what is the Solovay-Kitaev overhead this induces on gate count as a function of prime p?
basis: The paper claims 'the parameters of the gates can be calculated efficiently' but does not quantify how tight the tolerance must be. Since a single AA iteration is used, sensitivity to angle error is direct.
next_steps: Perturb alpha by epsilon in {1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-9}; simulate the AA step's success probability numerically; extract eps-vs-|1/4 - success| curve; combine with SK gate-count formula epsilon^(-log 3 / log 2 * something) to estimate rotation-synthesis budget.

q: At what prime order p does the Mosca-Zalka exact QFT become cheaper (in T-count or CNOT count) than a modern approximate QFT tuned to trace-distance error 1e-6 (e.g., truncated controlled-phase gates a la Coppersmith with Solovay-Kitaev)? Below that crossover, is there any real reason - beyond exactness as a matter of principle - to prefer the exact construction?
basis: The paper itself admits 'unlikely to be of any practical use' in the abstract. Twenty-plus years of subsequent QFT resource-optimisation work invites revisiting this. Our replication exercised only DFT_N and Qiskit's canonical (approximate for arbitrary N) QFT, not a resource-optimised approximate version.
next_steps: Compile both constructions for p in {31, 127, 509, 8191}; benchmark T-count using an existing tool (pyLIQUi, qiskit's transpiler with target basis {H, S, T, CNOT}); plot crossover; identify whether any current fault-tolerant application would prefer exact QFT.
